short: John Dee was a mathematician, astronomer, and occultist who served as a trusted advisor to Elizabeth I.
full:
Born on 13 July 1527, John Dee emerged as one of the most learned men of his generation, blending advanced mathematics and navigational science with alchemy and hermetic philosophy. He assembled one of the largest libraries in Europe at his home in Mortlake, which served as a crucial intellectual centre for scholars, courtiers, and navigators.

Dee provided vital astrological and geographical advice to the Queen and her explorers, notoriously coining the term "British Empire" to describe his vision of an English-led maritime dominance. His later life was increasingly consumed by controversial attempts to commune with angels, leading to his political marginalisation and poverty by the time of his death around 1609.
